archhint.body.text: The archetypes are the layer that configures the factory — each one applies a different weight to the domains and to Streamlining. Important: there is no “right” archetype for you — only the right one for the task. The same person can be a Code Surgeon on a code project and an Elite Bureaucrat on an executive report. Switch whenever you like: the ranking recalculates live.

welcome.p1.text: There is no “best AI” — there is the best AI for your work. Each tool is strong at some things and weak at others; the right question is not “which is smarter”, but “which delivers what I need, the way I need it”.

welcome.p2.text: This app exists to answer that question. Choose a professional profile that resembles yours, or customize one. In seconds, you will see a ranking of the 7 AIs most relevant on the market, ordered for this specific profile.

welcome.p3.text: Raw power is only half the story. The other half is friction: whether the AI already reads your data, delivers ready to use, and whether you can trust the source of what it states. The app weighs that too.

welcome.p4.text: Explore the profiles, play with the controls, and watch the recommendation change live.

origemnotas.p1.text: An AI's capability is not fixed – it changes fast, sometimes from one week to the next, as new models reach the market. That is why this Hub is not a frozen ranking, but a living instrument, periodically re-evaluated. When a rating moves, most of the time it is not an error correction: it is the world having changed.

origemnotas.p2.text: Each rating is born from the best evidence available for that specific capability – and that evidence is not uniform. It comes from three sources:

origemnotas.medido.desc.text: Where public, reliable benchmarks exist, the rating derives from them – this is the case for code engineering, chart and document analysis, massive context reading, and verifiability (grounding). A rating anchored in external, reproducible data.

origemnotas.aproximado.desc.text: In some capabilities there is no direct measure, but general benchmarks serve as an approximation. Logical reasoning, for example, is measured by tests that come close, without exactly capturing professional use. A rating informed by data, with a layer of interpretation.

origemnotas.especializada.desc.text: Some capabilities simply have no public benchmark – converting between levels of abstraction or maintaining brand identity consistency, for example. Here the rating is a declared expert assessment, not a measurement.

origemnotas.p3.text: How we choose benchmarks. Not just any leaderboard counts. A benchmark only qualifies if it is dynamic (refreshes its questions, so the result does not age), resistant to contamination (the questions were not in the model's training data – otherwise the score measures memory, not capability), and still able to separate the best models. Famous benchmarks that are saturated or contaminated are deliberately downgraded to historical status.

origemnotas.p4.text: What the rating is not. It is not a verdict of an absolute “best AI” – it is a snapshot, based on today's best evidence, of a specific capability. The final decision is yours: the safest path is to test the two or three candidates the Hub points to in real cases from your own work.

canon.canon-manifesto-intro.text.text: The Hub's conceptual core: why the most powerful tool isn't always the most recommended one. Operational friction (Streamlining) determines how much of an AI's raw power actually reaches your final deliverable.

canon.canon-falacia.text.text: This framework marks the definitive abandonment of the search for the “smartest AI” in favor of the search for the “most efficient AI.” In the real world, intelligence that can't be delivered in the right format, at the right time, with the right data is, for all practical purposes, nonexistent. The Synthetic IQ Fallacy occurs when we prioritize raw cognitive power (the AI's “IQ”) over interoperability. Here, intelligence is just one variable; efficiency is the multiplier.

canon.canon-fisica.text.text: The Hub operates under a new physics of systems. Power (P) is what the AI can do in isolation — its raw processing and logic capacity, measured by benchmark. Efficiency (E) is the capacity to manifest that power through the friction of human and corporate workflow. The real, measurable result is Effective Power, and the core principle is that power is multiplied by efficiency, never aggregated linearly with it — whether by sum, average, or weighting. A Power of 5.0 delivered at an Efficiency of 0.2 isn't worth 2.6 — the average of the two — it's worth 1.0, because friction doesn't discount the value, it strangles it.

canon.canon-meta-intro.text.text: The intellectual ‘engine room.’ These capabilities don't generate the final product, but they guarantee the integrity of the argument. This is where logical structuring, hypothesis validation, and thought architecture happen before any execution.

canon.canon-A.text.text: This use isn't just analysis nor just synthesis. It happens when you ask the AI to reconcile conflicting concepts between authors, schools, or frameworks; normalize terminology (e.g., equivalent concepts with different names); or integrate multiple sources into a single coherent vocabulary. It resolves conceptual ambiguities before any final production.

canon.canon-B.text.text: Here the AI isn't used to produce, but to check whether a line of reasoning “holdsup,” identify internal contradictions, point out logical leaps, and test whether a narrative holds under pressure. It's different from text review; it's a consistency audit.

canon.canon-C.title.text: C — Conversion between levels of abstraction

canon.canon-C.text.text: You use the AI to move up and down levels of abstraction with precision: Strategy ↔ operations, Framework ↔ process, Architecture ↔ implementation. This isn't generic “summarizing” or “expanding” — it's structural translation.

canon.canon-D.text.text: Creation of provisional matrices, hypothesis lists, and formal drafts that aren't meant for delivery, but for thinking better. These artifacts are neither creative drafts nor final outputs; they are temporary cognitive instruments.

canon.canon-disc-intro.text.text: The system's data-capture frontier. It expands the information base through active real-time external search or deep reading of complex legacy data — before any transformation takes place.

canon.canon-5-3.text.text: AI-based research assistants can scan academic and technical databases to synthesize the state of the art on a given topic. Unlike traditional search, the AI can read abstracts, cross-reference conclusions from different papers, and generate a structured literature review. The introduction of ‘Deep Research’ modes changed the nature of this use case. The AI can now fully read dozens of books and hundreds of articles simultaneously, drastically reducing hallucination through massive Grounding. Search has stopped being just about ‘finding the link’ and become about ‘synthesizing the knowledge contained in the link.’

canon.canon-5-4.title.text: 1.2 Massive, Thorough Summaries of Books and Complex Articles

canon.canon-5-4.text.text: Language models with expanded context windows (like Claude with 100k+ tokens or Gemini 1.5 Pro with 2M) allow the upload of entire technical books, long contracts, or hundred-page reports. The AI can then extract central arguments without losing nuance.

canon.canon-design-intro.text.text: The passage from conceptual abstraction to tangible visual artifact. It ensures the strategy doesn't remain cold text, but materializes into persuasive, visually consistent formats.

canon.canon-5-1.title.text: 1.4 Automated Generation of Slides and Presentations

canon.canon-5-1.text.text: Modern AI systems can generate complete presentations from text scripts, combining provided content with consistent visual themes. Tools built into productivity suites, like Microsoft Copilot, allow professional slides to be created directly from text documents and automatically apply visual elements aligned with brand identity. For example, Copilot in PowerPoint can reference organizational files (Word, PDF, etc.) to compose a presentation, as well as insert approved images from the company's library to ensure compliance with the visual identity guide. This avoids laborious manual formatting, since the AI can analyze text, key topics, images, and even logos, suggesting visual styles compatible with the presentation's theme. The result is a coherent slide structure, with consistent design across all pages, respecting the brand's color palette and typography. Importantly, the AI delivers a solid draft that can be refined by the user, combining automation with a human touch to adjust details when needed. In short, the AI drastically speeds up slide creation — studies show users can generate an initial deck 3–5 times faster than the manual method, with ever-higher visual quality and reduced need for editing.

canon.canon-5-2.text.text: The use of generative AI for images (such as DALL-E 3, Midjourney, and Adobe Firefly) enables the creation of visual assets that follow strict style guidelines. In the corporate context, this means training or instructing the AI to generate icons, illustrations, and diagrams that speak the same visual language as the brand, ensuring technical reports don't look like a visual patchwork. Consistency isn't just aesthetic; it's semiotic, ensuring the visual message reinforces the authority of the technical document.

canon.canon-5-5.title.text: 1.3 Multimodal Analysis of Photos, Videos, and Files

canon.canon-5-5.text.text: Multimodal capability (as in GPT-4 Vision or Gemini) allows the AI to ‘see’ and interpret images. This applies to reading complex charts in financial reports, converting whiteboard sketches into structured code, or analyzing video.

canon.canon-build-intro.text.text: The constructive and infrastructure capability. It separates the activity of designing from the activity of building executable, functional logical solutions.

canon.canon-5-6.title.text: 1.6 Web Application Generation and Coding Automation

canon.canon-5-6.text.text: AI agents specialized in code can generate not just isolated snippets, but entire web applications, data automation scripts, and functional user interfaces. This democratizes software engineering for data-analysis and management profiles, enabling the creation of custom tools (‘internal micro-SaaS’) to solve specific process pain points. The AI acts as a senior pair programmer, suggesting architecture, refactoring legacy code, and writing unit tests.

canon.canon-strat-intro.text.text: The missing link between technical data and executive decision-making. This capability integrates scattered inputs into a coherent view, translating technical complexity into business direction.

canon.canon-6-1.text.text: Use of AI to generate complete, structured, and well-argued analyses of markets, industries, business models, value chains, capabilities, processes, technologies, and frameworks — with or without external files — aimed at building a point of view, supporting decisions, and producing technical essays. In practice, it is the Connecting Axis between research, synthesis, design, and technology. It's the point where AI stops being a ‘reading tool’ and becomes a structured strategic-thinking tool. Typical outputs include complete strategic essays, market reports (TAM/SAM/SOM), comparative matrices, and executive narratives (points of view).

canon.canon-stream-intro.text.text: The efficiency layer that removes friction between machine intelligence and the human workflow. Unlike the five power domains, Streamlining is cross-cutting: it doesn't generate the product, but it determines whether that power can manifest without friction (the ‘Glue Work’).

canon.canon-7-1.text.text: Data Gravity isn't just an upload convenience; it's the elimination of the data-engineering (ETL) barrier for the end user. It defines the AI's competence to operate where the data already resides (Data in Place). Unlike systems that require manual file movement or complex API configuration, here the AI natively indexes SharePoint, the Graph API, or code repositories. It's not the AI “looking at” an isolated file; it's the AI “living inside the server,” maintaining context persistence and eliminating the need to migrate data for analysis.

canon.canon-7-2.text.text: This isn't about exporting text, it's about delivering a product. This capability measures the level of industrial finish of the deliverable. The question is: does the AI deliver an insight in Markdown that requires heavy manual formatting (high friction), or does it generate the final editable file (.pptx, .docx, .xlsx) rigorously respecting corporate templates and fonts? It's the fundamental difference between receiving a ‘smart draft’ that creates operational formatting work, and receiving a ‘ready artifact’ that creates immediate value and can be sent directly to the end client.

canon.canon-7-3.text.text: Here the AI isn't used to be creative, but to be auditable. It's the capability to build a trust architecture where every claim is granularly linked (line by line) to a verifiable primary source. This goes beyond generic ‘web search’; it's a reputational-risk mitigation mechanism. Without it, strategic synthesis (2.1) becomes just a hallucinated opinion; with it, it becomes a safe basis for signing off on executive decisions and fiduciary duties, enabling full traceability of information.

matrix.gemini.7.3.text: Multimodality enables visual verification and Deep Think reduces hallucinations, though it can lose nuance in the middle of massive contexts.

matrix.claude.B.text: Competes with o1 via visible ‘thinking blocks’; superior at validating qualitative arguments and ethical nuance, being more ‘Socratic.’

matrix.claude.C.text: The ‘Universal Translator.’ Unmatched at converting technical specifications into executive summaries while keeping tone and intent precise.

matrix.claude.D.text: Market benchmark. The Artifacts interface lets you ‘build’ thinking visually with diagrams and interactive apps in a dedicated window.

matrix.claude.5.2.text: Text-only; doesn't generate raster images or handle graphic visual identity.

matrix.claude.5.3.text: Excellent analyst, limited researcher. Depends on configured tools, without a robust autonomous native browser.

matrix.claude.5.4.text: 200k-token recall is very precise, but inferior to Google's volumetric capacity.

matrix.claude.5.5.text: Great for photos and documents, but lacks native video-analysis support.

matrix.claude.6.1.text: The Trusted Strategist. Balances cutting-edge reasoning, C-level writing nuance, and a robust privacy posture.

matrix.claude.7.1.text: Data isolation: privacy focus means few native connectors; performs best on what's supplied in context.

matrix.claude.7.2.text: Artifacts deliver ready-to-use code/HTML, but there's no native generation of corporate .pptx/.docx; document handoff is limited.

matrix.claude.7.3.text: High logical reliability and an honest ‘I don't know’ posture, but lacks native search to anchor facts in primary sources.

matrix.chatgpt.B.text: Keeps the crown for pure reasoning. Unmatched at formal logic and fallacy detection through deep verification chains.

matrix.chatgpt.C.text: Robust and competent, but requires more prompt engineering to nail the exact tone for sensitive executive communication compared to Claude.

matrix.chatgpt.D.text: Robust for writing and inline coding, but visual-element integration and fluidity are still a step behind Anthropic.

matrix.chatgpt.5.1.text: Still relies on juggling Python or standalone DALL-E; lacks a native ‘text to deck’ solution.

matrix.chatgpt.5.2.text: Image 1.5 (DALL-E 3) maintains fidelity to storytelling and complex prompts.

matrix.chatgpt.5.3.text: Powerful agentic capability, but cohesive, cited-report integration is still inferior to Perplexity.

matrix.chatgpt.5.4.text: A 128k window is good, but suffers from ‘loss in the middle’ on massive works.

matrix.chatgpt.5.5.text: GPT-4o Vision excels at OCR of complex tables and handwritten diagrams.

matrix.chatgpt.5.6.text: Logic Specialist. The o3 model is unbeatable for complex mathematical algorithms, but the overall developer experience (DX) loses fluidity to Claude/Copilot.

matrix.chatgpt.6.1.text: The Logic Engine. Indispensable for scenario modeling and ‘Game Theory’ applied to business.

matrix.chatgpt.7.1.text: No native corporate connectors; relies on manual upload. Research is web-first, external to the company's repository.

matrix.chatgpt.7.2.text: Good artifact and Canvas generation, delivering reusable structures, though final Office polish still needs manual adjustment.

matrix.chatgpt.7.3.text: Middling grounding: hallucinates in highly technical contexts without anchored sources, requiring human verification.

matrix.copilot.5.3.text: Brings deep research into a secure environment, but the Bing index can be less comprehensive for technical niches.

matrix.copilot.5.4.text: Frequently cuts off long texts due to token limits in the commercial interface.

matrix.copilot.5.5.text: Uses integrated GPT-4o; very good for analysts working with screenshots.

help.intro.text: This dashboard isn't just a list of tools; it's a decision engine calibrated to find the best AI tool for your professional profile. Follow the logical flow below to get the most out of this app.

help.s1.p.text: Don't start with the tools, start with your goal. AI capabilities are organized into six domains — five power domains plus one cross-cutting enabler:

help.s1.list.text:
• Thinking (Reasoning): planning, critiquing, validating, and structuring.
  • Discovering (Discovery): researching, mass reading, and ingesting data.
  • Designing (Materialization): slides, visual identity, and multimodality.
  • Building (Construction): generating code and applications.
  • Integrating (Strategy): synthesizing everything into an executive decision.
  • Streamlining (Enabler): reducing friction between the AI and your workflow — data access, delivery format, and trustworthiness.

help.s1.example.text: Scenario: Ana needs to create a launch strategy for a digital bank. She's not just looking for “a chatbot”: she needs the AI technology best suited to the job. So she opens the app and looks at the capabilities in the “What an AI delivers” section, and realizes her project requires three of them: 1.3 In-Depth Academic and Technical Research (to read banking regulations), B — Logical validation, internal consistency, and stress-testing (to test her pricing model), and 1.1 Automated Generation of PowerPoint Presentations (for the final presentation).

help.s2.p.text: Understand where each capability fits into your real workflow, from Input (research and curation), through Process (logical validation), to Output (final delivery).

help.s2.example.text:
Ana looks at the Pipeline board and maps out her flow:
1. Input: First, she'll use the 1.3 In-Depth Academic and Technical Research capability to scan Central Bank regulations.
2. Process: Then, she'll use the B — Logical validation, internal consistency, and stress-testing meta-case to find holes in the thesis.
3. Output: Finally, she'll use the 1.1 Automated Generation of PowerPoint Presentations capability to turn the text into a slide deck.

help.s3.p.text: This is the most important step. Choose one of the seven professional archetypes or manually adjust the five domain sliders (Thinking, Discovering, Designing, Building, Integrating) according to how relevant each is to your work.

help.s3.list.text:
• How much does each domain matter for your deliverable?
  • And Streamlining: are you more of an Artisan (you want raw power and assemble the result by hand) or an Operator (you want the deliverable ready, with no friction)?

help.s3.note.text: The Streamlining slider controls how much friction penalizes the ranking. The system reacts in real time.

help.s3.example.text: In the Decision tab, Ana raises Thinking and Discovering (she needs logical precision and to scan regulations) and also Designing, since the final deliverable is a slide deck. She keeps Building low, since she won't be writing code. Since she needs the PowerPoint ready to go for leadership, she pushes the Streamlining slider toward Operator — signaling that manual-formatting friction should count against AIs that only deliver raw text.

help.s4.p1.text: Based on the defined profile, the Decision Engine calculates each AI's score and builds the ranking. Each AI receives an Effective Score per domain — raw power multiplied by that domain's Efficiency Factor — and the final score is the weighted average across your sliders.

help.s4.p2.text: Power × Efficiency: a powerful but high-friction AI can lose to a less powerful one that delivers ready to use. Hover over each ranking card to see the breakdown (P, F, D, and E) domain by domain. When two leaders are within 0.001 of each other, both receive the Technical Tie badge.

help.s4.example.text: The Engine processes Ana's hybrid profile (high logic + high visual delivery + Operator bias). The ranking reflects that combination: pure-text tools drop because their low Format Continuity (3.2) is penalized by friction, while Copilot M365 and Gemini 3.1 Pro rise for delivering closer to ready-to-use. Hovering over the card, Ana sees that GPT-5.5 Pro has great power, but loses Effective Score in the Designing domain due to format handoff.

help.s5.list.text:

  • Check the Library (Section 6) to read the canonical definitions of each capability.

help.s5.example.text: Ana doesn't want surprises. She goes to the Technical Audit (Section 5) and specifically checks the slide-generation capability in the matrix. She notices that ChatGPT has visual limitations (a low score on 1.1 Automated Generation of PowerPoint Presentations), while MS Copilot scores at the top on this item. This validates her choice of a hybrid workflow.

tags.p1.text: In the context of the AI Strategy Hub app, these tags represent each tool's primary nature — that is, at which stage of the “Production Pipeline” (Input → Process → Output) it shines brightest.

tags.card1.text:
1. Input

What it is: Tools specialized in searching, filtering, and bringing real-world information into your workflow.

Focus: Research (grounding), fact-checking, and autonomous web navigation.

AIs in this category:
Perplexity: Acts as a conversational search engine, perfect for replacing Google and bringing cited sources.
Manus: An agent that browses the web to carry out tasks and find scattered data.

tags.card2.text:
2. Reasoning

What it is: Tools focused on the "Processing" stage. They are the densest "brains," ideal for handling complex logic, coding, structuring arguments, and theoretical validation.

Focus: Pure logic, mathematics, software architecture, and complex/nuanced writing.

AIs in this category:
GPT: Versatile and multimodal, with reasoning modes to reduce logical hallucinations.
Claude: Benchmark for logic, clean coding (Artifacts), and textual nuance.
DeepSeek: Focused on rigorous mathematical and logical reasoning via chain of thought.

tags.card3.text:
3. Delivery

What it is: Tools geared toward "Output" and final production. They’re best at packaging content into a usable format (slides, formatted documents, images, email/Office integration).

Focus: Multimodality (viewing and creating images/video), integration with ecosystems (Google/Microsoft), and generation of final artifacts.

AIs in this category:
Gemini: Strong integration with Google Workspace and a native 1M-token context for reading documents and producing content.
Copilot M365: Specialized in delivering native Word documents and PowerPoint slides within the Microsoft ecosystem.

It doesn't produce the final deliverable, but it ensures the logic behind it is sound.

art.fio.hero.kick.text: Quando é Melhor com IA · Gonçalo Marques

art.fio.hero.title.text: The brilliant lawyer who never files the brief.

art.fio.hero.lede.text: Picture a lawyer of exceptional intelligence who refuses to file briefs in the format the court accepts, requiring the client to transcribe every idea by hand. The competence is real and measurable. And completely irrelevant to whoever needs the result.

art.fio.hero.quote.text: This is what happens when you use a state-of-the-art AI and still end the day redoing what it produced.

art.fio.hero.bridge.text: This discomfort has a name and a cause. And someone has confronted it with method.

art.fio.livro.h.text: The book that describes this problem

art.fio.livro.p0.text: Quando é Melhor com IA gives this discomfort a name, explains its cause and proposes a method for working around it. Everything on this page comes from the book.

art.fio.livro.s.text: Professional augmentation through AI use. From Strategic Analysis to Technical Production.

art.fio.livro.v2.text: Anyone who produces analysis, decisions or technical deliverables

art.fio.livro.p1.text: Its stated purpose is to guide the professional in applying AI with rigour, accountability and method to the work of producing and applying knowledge. The focus is on raising the quality of technical output, of complex information analysis and of strategic decision support – advanced use, not casual or purely theoretical uses.

art.fio.livro.p2.text: To that end it separates three things usually bundled together: the AI's technical capabilities, the use cases that mobilise them, and the cross-cutting functions running through any task. Everything that follows grows out of that separation.

art.fio.livro.p3.text: The sections below walk through the book's central argument, from the problem it names to the method it proposes.

art.fio.falacia.p1.text: The book names the discomfort: believing that a high score on reasoning tests translates automatically into delivered productivity. It does not.

art.fio.falacia.p2.text: An engineer who can solve arbitrarily complex algorithms but cannot read his own company's repository has real intellectual power. And irrelevant power. Power that does not show up as delivery is, for the user, non-existent.

art.fio.grandezas.eye.text: Here the argument splits in two

art.fio.grandezas.p1.text: Power and efficiency are not two points on the same scale. They are independent axes. An AI can have plenty of power and little efficiency – the lawyer who never files – or the reverse: everything delivered ready, with little to say.

art.fio.grandezas.c1p.text: What the AI can do: reason, synthesise, analyse. This is what public benchmarks measure.

art.fio.grandezas.c2p.text: How much of that power reaches you without being lost on the way. No benchmark measures this.

art.fio.grandezas.p2.text: From here on, every concept in the book belongs to one of the two threads. They only meet again at the end.

art.fio.metacasos.p.text: Functions the AI performs backstage in almost any task, and which until recently had no name. Recognising them lets you break a task down before you start.

art.fio.metacasos.ap.text: Comparing the sources, choosing equivalent terms and assembling a common frame. It is pre-analytical: it prepares the conceptual ground everything else will be built on.

art.fio.metacasos.bp.text: Auditing a line of reasoning: internal contradictions, unjustified leaps. It does not produce content, it audits it.

art.fio.metacasos.cp.text: Translating between the strategic, tactical and operational levels (processes and implementation). This is what lets one analysis serve both the board and the technical team.

art.fio.metacasos.dp.text: Provisional matrices, tables, sketches and the like that never reach the final deliverable, but exist to think better during the process.

art.fio.analise.p1.text: Chapter 7 of the book covers strategic-synthesis use and lists the components you must ask for, precisely so the analysis does not come back incomplete through the asker's omission: market, benchmark, value chain, capabilities, processes, technologies, frameworks.

art.fio.analise.p2.text: The flow described is an AI operating as a junior consultant, with you as the senior consultant who directs and reviews.

art.fio.cola.p1.text: Copying a model's output into an editor. Reformatting a table for the company spreadsheet. Re-uploading a file the AI should have reached on its own. Each of these bridges is lost energy, and each loss brings delay and risk of error.

art.fio.cola.p2.text: The chapter's thesis is that this friction is not an implementation detail. It is a first-order economic variable – with consequences for return on investment, for vendor lock-in, and for opacity, when excessive fluidity erodes the very traceability it should protect.

art.fio.eixos.p.text: Efficiency is not a single number. It breaks down into three independent dimensions, each answering a distinct question about how the AI meets real work.

art.fio.eixos.a1p.text: Does the AI operate where the data already lives, or does it require you to extract and carry it manually?

art.fio.eixos.a2p.text: Is the output a draft to be rebuilt, or a finished artefact in the format it will be consumed in?

art.fio.eixos.a3p.text: Is every factual claim traceable to a source? A synthesis without auditability is merely an opinion.

art.fio.alucinacao.p1.text: The book's founding principle, and the most uncomfortable for being so direct: every factual claim the AI makes is suspect until proven otherwise. A human expert enjoys presumed credibility; the AI gets no such benefit of the doubt on matters of fact.

art.fio.alucinacao.p2.text: The book likens this to zero defect in quality management. Absolute zero may be unreachable, but the value lies in never accepting an error without having confronted it. That is where casual use parts ways with professional use: the first settles for most things being right.

art.fio.alucinacao.cp.text: If a deliverable goes out with an error, the fault is not the AI's – it belongs to whoever reviewed and approved it. The AI carries no legal liability. Whoever signs, does.

art.fio.arquetipos.p.text: No professional uses every capability in the same proportion, nor demands the same fluidity for every task. Hence the gallery of archetypes – and some will probably sound familiar.

art.fio.arquetipos.a1.w.text: Strategy consultants, M&A analysts, scenario planners, executive advisors

art.fio.arquetipos.a1.p.text: Uses the AI as a dialectical partner. What matters is the quality of the reasoning delivered in running text; polished formatting is irrelevant next to the robustness of the argument.

art.fio.arquetipos.a2.w.text: Regulatory compliance, corporate lawyers, project managers, process analysts

art.fio.arquetipos.a2.p.text: The last-mile professional, for whom zero formatting error is not a luxury but a requirement. Any residual copy-and-paste is a failure of the system.

art.fio.arquetipos.a3.w.text: Journalists, due diligence analysts, risk auditors, fraud investigators

art.fio.arquetipos.a3.p.text: Extracts truth from oceans of raw data and rejects any claim without a link to a real source. This is where Zero Hallucination shows up most literally.

art.fio.arquetipos.a4.w.text: Product managers, marketing directors, launch leads, PMO managers

art.fio.arquetipos.a4.p.text: Turns abstract business visions into decks, visual reports and video. High input volume, output that has to be flawless.

art.fio.arquetipos.a5.w.text: Large-systems consultants, banking systems engineers, critical infrastructure

art.fio.arquetipos.a5.p.text: Reads and diagnoses massive systems and sprawling documentation – work that demands colossal context windows, on pain of losing critical dependencies.

art.fio.arquetipos.q.text: The profiles are not sealed compartments: the same professional moves between identities depending on the day's task.

art.fio.artesao.q.text: Which side does this piece of work benefit from?

art.fio.artesao.p1.text: On the left, you value the process and demand full control: the AI supplies the raw intellectual material and final assembly stays deliberately manual. On the right, you want the finished product, and any manual step registers as a system failure.

art.fio.artesao.p2.text: The right position depends on the nature of the task, not on a generic preference for more or less automation. Maturity is not choosing a side once and for all, but recognising, for each piece of work, which side or point on the spectrum it benefits from.

art.fio.mapa.p1.text: What sets the book apart, in its own preface's words: rather than cataloguing tools, it builds a map that separates the AI's technical capabilities from the use cases that mobilise them, and both from the cross-cutting functions running through any task.

art.fio.mapa.p2.text: It is not a book about programming, and it demands no technical background – there are three reading tracks: executive, technical and consultative. Nor is it a book about the future of AI: it does not speculate, does not warn of existential risk, does not catalogue tools that will be obsolete within a year.

art.fio.cta.p.text: A vocabulary and a method for deciding, task by task, when it is better with AI – and how to do it without giving up what is non-negotiable: the quality, reliability, ethics and coherence of what you sign.

art.fio.cta.fine.text:
Professional augmentation through AI use.
From Strategic Analysis to Technical Production.

art.cem.hero.kick.text: Quando é Melhor com IA · Gonçalo Marques

art.cem.hero.title.text: A hundred books, three surveys, one question.

art.cem.hero.lede.text: I asked three artificial intelligences to survey, each entirely on its own, everything published about AI. Oxford references, IMF reports, McKinsey lists, Amazon bestsellers, the Brazilian editorial press. About a hundred works.

art.cem.hero.quote.text: They disagreed. And it was in the disagreement that what I was looking for showed up.

art.cem.hero.bridge.text: This discomfort has a name and a cause. And someone has confronted it with method.

art.cem.experimento.h.text: I didn't ask for opinion. I asked for a survey.

art.cem.experimento.p.text: What exists, where it's published, and which theme comes up most often. Each system received the same request and ran the search on its own.

art.cem.divergencia.h.text: Each one pointed to a different theme as the most frequent in the market.

art.cem.porque.p1.text: Each had looked at a different shelf of the same bookstore. Academia selects what informs public policy. The bestseller list records what the professional buys to use on Monday. The business press records what the executive reads to decide on a budget.

art.cem.porque.p2.text: Three cuts, three answers. That's when the question changed: instead of looking for what the three agreed on, I started looking for what none of them found.

art.cem.ponto.p.text: Two of them, working over collections that barely overlap, arrived on their own at the same result: there's a question no book answers.

art.cem.problema.h.text: Why does the AI you chose still hand back hours of rework?

art.cem.problema.p.text: The AI that tops every best-model list still returns raw material that takes hours to turn into something presentable. The answer is that knowing and delivering are two independent scales. Public benchmarks measure only the first. The second decides your day — and charges a tax that shows up in no productivity report.

art.cem.evidencia.p0.text: The numbers already exist, and they all point to the same place.

art.cem.evidencia.s1p.text: of corporate generative-AI pilots produce measurable financial impact.

art.cem.evidencia.s2p.text: workers tracked across 7,000 workplaces showed no significant effect on wages or hours.

art.cem.evidencia.s2src.text: Anders Humlum and Emilie Vestergaard, National Bureau of Economic Research · May 2025

art.cem.evidencia.q.text: The data described the phenomenon. It still needed a name.

art.cem.livro.h.text: Written in that gap between knowing and delivering.

art.cem.livro.p1.text: Quando é Melhor com IA is not a warning about the future or a catalogue of tools — AI capabilities change too fast for that, and the book treats them deliberately in the abstract. It classifies AI use into four categories — operational, analytical, creative and strategic-synthetic — and shows, for each type of input and output (text, spreadsheet, code, image), what to check before trusting the result. It also describes seven professional profiles, from the one who codes and audits software to the one who needs documents formatted with zero margin for error, with the combination of capabilities each one requires.

art.cem.livro.p2.text: It's this map of profiles that the AI Strategy Hub, a free tool separate from the book, uses to recommend which specific AI applies to yours.

art.cem.cta.p.text: You've already switched AIs, and the rework stayed the same. Switching was never the answer.

art.dez.p1.h.text: Start with the problem, not the tool

art.dez.p1.p1.text: Before opening any AI application, state clearly what needs to be solved and check that this use serves a real goal of your work. The opening question is never "which AI should I use?" but "what result do I need to deliver, and why?".

art.dez.p1.cite1.text: Ch. 11.3 · Final guidelines for advanced and responsible use of AI

art.dez.p1.ex1.text: Before adopting an AI solution, clarify the problem to be solved and check whether the application makes sense within the larger strategy. AI should not be used out of fashion, but to meet defined objectives.

art.dez.p2.h.text: Classify the task by nature and by competence

art.dez.p2.p1.text: Place the work in one of the four categories of use (operational, analytical, creative or strategic-synthetic) and then identify which domain of competence it mobilises (Thinking, Discovering, Designing, Building or Integrating). This double classification tells you what kind of benefit to expect and which precautions matter.

art.dez.p2.axis_p.text: The four categories are defined in Ch. 2.1 and developed in concrete cases in Chs. 6 and 7. The five domains are defined in Ch. 3.6, under the general conceptual map of Ch. 3.1.

art.dez.p2.cite1.text: Ch. 2.1 · Criteria for classifying uses of AI

art.dez.p2.ex1.text: The book adopts a canonical classification that distinguishes levels or modes of AI use in four main categories: operational, analytical, creative and strategic-synthetic.

art.dez.p2.ex2.text: By classifying each use case in these categories, the work establishes clear criteria of comparison – for instance, operational cases are judged by the immediate efficiency gain, while strategic cases are judged by the depth and reliability of the analysis produced.

art.dez.p2.cite2.text: Ch. 3.6 · Two complementary lenses: from categories of use to domains of competence

art.dez.p2.ex3.text: Where the first lens asks "what kind of use is this?", the second asks "what kind of competence does this use demand?".

art.dez.p2.ex4.text: The five domains of competence – Thinking (cognitive reasoning), Discovering (discovery and ingestion), Designing (visual materialisation), Building (engineering and construction) and Integrating (strategy and decision) – do not revoke the four categories of use; they project them onto the plane of the competences each task exercises.

art.dez.p2.q1.text: A sixth layer, transversal and non-disciplinary, accompanies these five: enablement, or Streamlining, defined in Ch. 3.6 and developed in Ch. 5, which is the subject of Step 7.

art.dez.p3.h.text: Prepare the right point of entry

art.dez.p3.p1.text: No result is born from a vacuum: each domain consumes reality through an input of its own – curated sources, a code repository, visual references, business context. Gather and organise that input before asking for any output, because the modality of the input determines the nature of what the AI can produce.

art.dez.p3.cite1.text: Ch. 3.7 · The fractal symmetry of the production cycle

art.dez.p3.ex1.text: The first is essential ingestion: nothing is created from a vacuum. Every professional identity has a specific point of entry through which it consumes reality – text, image or code – before it can turn it into a product. The second is strict dependency: the modality of the input rigidly determines the nature of the output.

art.dez.p3.cite2.text: Ch. 11.2 · Condition of excellence: quality of input data

art.dez.p3.ex2.text: Feed the AI only with quality data – just as poor raw materials compromise a product, incorrect or biased inputs will make the AI produce unreliable results.

art.dez.p4.h.text: Ground the AI in verifiable sources

art.dez.p4.p1.text: With files available, instruct the AI to use them preferentially and to flag contradictions between them. Without files, require every number or fact to come with a source or be declared an estimate, and set the temporal and geographic scope. In both cases, ask for the premises to be made explicit.

art.dez.p4.ex1.text: When drafting, consider the data provided in the files (relatório_financeiro.pdf, processos.xlsx). Use this factual information preferentially, avoiding unfounded assumptions. If there are contradictions between the sources, highlight them.

art.dez.p4.ex2.text: If you cite specific numbers or facts, mention the source or indicate that it is an estimate based on general knowledge.

art.dez.p5.h.text: Steer the interaction through the four metacases

art.dez.p5.p1.text: Break the work down into cognitive functions and ask for them in sequence: first the curation and integration of sources (Metacase A – Curation, normalisation and integration of knowledge), then critique and logic testing (Metacase B – Logical validation and conceptual stress test), then translation to the audience's level of abstraction (Metacase C – Conversion between levels of abstraction) and, finally, intermediate artefacts such as outlines, matrices and checklists (Metacase D – Generation of intermediate thinking artefacts). Ask for the outline before the final product.

art.dez.p5.axis_p.text: Ch. 4 is entirely devoted to the metacases: Ch. 4.1 establishes their transversal character, Chs. 4.2 to 4.5 define them one by one, Ch. 4.6 shows the sequence in use and Ch. 7.4 deals with their integration with the strategic cases.

art.dez.p5.card_h1.text: Curation, normalisation and integration of knowledge

art.dez.p5.card_p1.text: Reconcile the sources before any drafting.

art.dez.p5.card_h2.text: Logical validation and conceptual stress test

art.dez.p5.card_p2.text: Ask for the critique of the alternatives and the test against an adverse scenario.

art.dez.p5.card_p3.text: Translate the result to the level of the audience that will read it.

art.dez.p5.card_p4.text: Outlines, matrices and lists before the final product.

art.dez.p5.cite1.text: Ch. 4.2 · Metacase A – Curation, normalisation and integration of knowledge

art.dez.p5.ex1.text: its goal is not merely to present new content, but to prepare the conceptual ground on which any content will be generated.

art.dez.p5.cite2.text: Ch. 4.3 · Metacase B – Logical validation and conceptual stress test

art.dez.p5.ex2.text: The second metacase refers to using AI to check the logical robustness, internal consistency and conceptual soundness of arguments, plans or structures.

art.dez.p5.cite3.text: Ch. 4.4 · Metacase C – Conversion between levels of abstraction

art.dez.p5.ex3.text: the AI's ability to translate content from one level of abstraction to another while keeping the information precise and relevant.

art.dez.p5.cite4.text: Ch. 4.5 · Metacase D – Generation of intermediate thinking artefacts

art.dez.p5.ex4.text: using AI to produce provisional cognitive artefacts, which are not in themselves the desired final result, but instruments to help think through, organise or advance the final solution.

art.dez.p5.cite5.text: Ch. 4.6 · Practical identification of the metacases in action

art.dez.p5.ex5.text: Right, first I will ask for an integration of the sources (metacase A), then the generation of alternatives and a critique of each (metacase B), then request the translation of the best alternative into an operational plan (metacase C) and use the AI to assemble a final checklist (metacase D).

art.dez.p5.cite6.text: Ch. 4.1 · The role of the metacases as a transversal layer

art.dez.p5.ex6.text: has the AI already curated the sources adequately? Is it worth asking it to test the logic of the conclusion? Should I ask the AI for an outline of ideas (an intermediate artefact) before the final answer?

art.dez.p6.h.text: Iterate, refine and have the AI audit itself

art.dez.p6.p1.text: Treat the first answer as a draft. Refine it through explicit feedback, without starting over, and use the AI itself (or a second instance) to look for inconsistencies in what it produced.

art.dez.p6.cite1.text: Ch. 3.4 · Patterns of interaction, iteration and validation

art.dez.p6.ex1.text: using AI effectively is not a one-off act of "ask and receive"; it involves an interactive cycle of fine-tuning and validation.

art.dez.p6.ex2.text: careful users use AI not only to generate content, but also to check it. This may mean using the AI to critically analyse the very answer it gave ("Find possible inconsistencies in the text above").

art.dez.p7.h.text: Choose the tool by friction, not by power alone

art.dez.p7.p1.text: Assess the AI on two independent axes: how much it can do, which is power, and how much of that reaches you without glue work, which is efficiency. Check the three axes of enablement – Data Gravity, Format Continuity and Reliability and Verifiability – and remember that friction weighs little in reasoning tasks and heavily in execution tasks.

art.dez.p7.p2.text: Decide, task by task, where on the spectrum between Artisan and Operator you want to stand.

art.dez.p7.spec_q.text: With each piece of work, recognise which side of the spectrum it benefits from.

art.dez.p7.ex1.text: Friction, in other words, does not erode power uniformly: it is absorbed at little cost by the reasoning domains and amplified, almost without damping, by the execution domains.

art.dez.p7.cite2.text: Ch. 5.7 · The spectrum from Artisan to Operator

art.dez.p7.ex2.text: the mature user's task is not to pick a side once and for all, but to recognise, with each new piece of work, which side of the spectrum that specific work benefits from.

art.dez.p7.p3.text: The archetypes – identities of use that weight the five domains of competence and sit at a specific point of the Artisan-Operator spectrum – give you the vocabulary to turn "I need a good AI" into an operational requirement.

art.dez.p7.cite3.text: Ch. 8.9 · Synthesis: from identity to calibration

art.dez.p7.ex3.text: I need an AI with the enablement configuration of the Signal Hunter (the archetype of the investigator who extracts informational truth from oceans of raw data and web pages, demanding full traceability and rejecting any synthetic claim without a clear link to a real source)

art.dez.p8.h.text: Protect sensitive data and intellectual property

art.dez.p8.p1.text: Never enter confidential data into a public or unapproved tool; anonymise before submitting; review generated code from a security standpoint; avoid requests "in the style" of protected works and check generated images by reverse search.

art.dez.p8.cite1.text: Ch. 9.4 · Privacy, security and sensitive data

art.dez.p8.ex1.text: The first is never to enter confidential data into a public or unapproved tool. When the service is necessary, prefer those that offer a no-retention clause. The second is to anonymise before submitting.

art.dez.p8.cite2.text: Ch. 9.5 · Intellectual property and responsible use

art.dez.p8.ex2.text: The preventive caution is to avoid requests that explicitly infringe third-party rights – generating content "in the style" of a protected work, for instance – and, when generating images or logos, to check by reverse search that the result does not come too close to something that already exists.

art.dez.p9.h.text: Validate as a human and apply the checklist before delivering

art.dez.p9.p1.text: Do the technical review (facts, calculations, clarity) and the critical review (tone, implications, alignment with the intent). Then run the deliverable through the quality checklist.

art.dez.p9.arch_who.text: Ch. 9.6 · each item takes "OK" or "Adjustment needed"

art.dez.p9.arch_p.text: Fact and source checking · Integrity and completeness · Logical coherence · Clarity and style · Spelling, grammar and formatting · Privacy and sensitivity · Originality and intellectual property · Security in technical deliverables · Ethical adequacy · Project-specific criteria.

art.dez.p9.cite1.text: Ch. 9.2 · Zero hallucination: the stance of proactive scepticism

art.dez.p9.ex1.text: The practical rule that follows is direct: every factual claim by the AI is suspect until proven otherwise.

art.dez.p9.cite2.text: Ch. 9.3 · Human validation, critical review and the limits of automation

art.dez.p9.ex2.text: The right stance is not "if the AI said it, it's right", but "it may be right, and I will check".

art.dez.p9.ex3.text: If a deliverable goes out with an error, the fault is not "the AI's": it lies with whoever reviewed and approved it.

art.dez.p9.ex4.text: There is a virtuous side effect: whoever knows the review will demand sources already instructs the AI to provide them; whoever knows they will go through plagiarism checking already tells the AI to rephrase more.

art.dez.p10.h.text: Record, trace and feed continuous improvement

art.dez.p10.p1.text: Keep the prompts that worked, version the answers and keep what the AI changed traceable – fluidity without a record erodes auditability. Turn recurring failures into new checklist items.

art.dez.p10.cite1.text: Ch. 3.4 · Patterns of interaction, iteration and validation

art.dez.p10.ex1.text: practices such as recording the prompts used (especially if they were carefully developed) and saving the answers in a versioned format, or using tools that allow conversations to be resumed and decisions taken on the basis of the AI to be justified, are recommended.

art.dez.p10.cite2.text: Ch. 5.6 · The economics of friction: ROI, vendor lock-in and opacity

art.dez.p10.ex2.text: Extreme fluidity, paradoxically, can erode the very trust that Streamlining is supposed to protect, if it is not accompanied by a discipline of traceability.

art.dez.p10.cite3.text: Ch. 10.4 · Guidelines for future evolution without loss of integrity

art.dez.p10.ex3.text: a recurring failure identified in one project becomes a new checklist item for the next ones. Integrity, then, is not static – it is maintained by a cycle of review, not by a fixed snapshot.

art.dez.sintese.p1.text: The ten steps describe a single movement: start from a real problem, classify it by the nature of the task and the competence it demands, feed the AI with the right input and ground it in verifiable sources, steer the interaction through the transversal functions of curation, validation, abstraction and outlining, refine in cycles, choose the tool by what it actually delivers and not by what it promises, protect what is confidential, validate with human judgement before signing and record everything so that the method evolves.

art.dez.sintese.p2.text: The book sums up this cycle as the union of artificial intelligence and human intelligence guided by sound principles (Ch. 11.3) – AI amplifies the capacity of whoever operates it, but does not replace judgement (Ch. 9.3). It is when the professional keeps the problem ahead of the tool, the source ahead of fluency and the review ahead of speed that the answer to the title's question stops being abstract and becomes operational. These are the conditions that establish when it's better with AI.

art.dez.cta.p.text: A vocabulary and a method for deciding, task by task, when it is better with AI – and how to do it without giving up what is non-negotiable: the quality, reliability, ethics and coherence of what you sign.

art.rod.hero.title.text: Before and after: the right AI for your kind of work.

art.rod.hero.lede.text: Rodrigo, 44, strategic planning manager. He has used artificial intelligence for two years. He would say, if asked, that he uses it well.

art.rod.hero.bridge.text: One day before, one day after.

art.rod.partida.h.text: He is not wrong. He has no map.

art.rod.partida.p1.text: Rodrigo asks the AI for things and gets things. The cycle works well enough not to raise an alarm – and badly enough to cost dearly every day, in a currency nobody accounts for.

art.rod.partida.q.text: What follows is one of his working days. Then the same day – six weeks later.

art.rod.falacia.p1.text: Rodrigo chose the AI that leads the lists of best models. He never put the assumption into words – it simply organises his choices.

art.rod.falacia.pt1.text: The genius that does not deliver

art.rod.falacia.p2.text: Knowing and delivering are not the same scale. They are two independent scales – and public performance tests measure only the first.

art.rod.pedido.h.text: He never asked the AI to think.

art.rod.pedido.p1.text: Two years of use, hundreds of requests, all with the same shape – a finished product for someone to read.

art.rod.pedido.i1.text: Write a report on the competitor's move.

art.rod.pedido.q.text: None of them was about thinking. They were all about delivering.

art.rod.pedido.p2.text: The request determines what you get. Whoever only asks for the finished product never discovers that the tool also serves the step before – the one in which the problem is still being formulated.

art.rod.fonte.p1.text: The director points at a slide. Rodrigo cannot answer. He goes back to the AI, asks for the source, receives a bibliographic reference that sounds impeccable – and does not exist.

art.rod.fonte.q.text: Casual use settles for most things being right. Professional use pursues factual exactness.

art.rod.virada.h.text: Effort was not lacking. A map was.

art.rod.virada.p1.text: All work with AI exercises five domains of competence. Inside each one live the concrete capabilities – researching, building slides, programming, synthesising.

art.rod.virada.d6d.text: a layer that runs through the five and decides whether the result arrives ready or raw

art.rod.virada.p2.text: The flow layer asks three questions, and only three:

art.rod.virada.q1.text: Does the AI reach my data where it lives?

art.rod.virada.q2.text: Does the file come out ready to use?

art.rod.virada.q3.text: Does every claim come with a checkable source?

art.rod.arq.h.text: He was not who he thought he was.

art.rod.arq.p1.text: An archetype is an identity of use: the characteristic proportion in which a kind of work mobilises the five domains – and how much it demands from the flow layer. Rodrigo took himself for one. He was another.

art.rod.arq.t1.text: “Someone who turns business vision into material ready for consumption.”

art.rod.arq.t2.text: “Someone who builds the thesis that guides the decision.”

art.rod.arq.p2.text: The slide deck is the packaging. The thesis is the substance. Rodrigo demanded visual finish from his tools – when what his work requires is a solid argument.

art.rod.arq.p3.text: The ends of this spectrum are called Artisan – who accepts manual work in exchange for control – and Operator, who treats any touch-up as a failure. The right place on it depends on the task, not on preference.

art.rod.arq.nota.text: Quando é Melhor com IA, by Gonçalo Marques – the method for choosing and using AI professionally that underpins this series. Available on Amazon.

art.rod.pensar.p1.text: Before asking for any text, Rodrigo started asking for something nobody will read: which axes the analysis demands, which questions he should be asking himself, which risks are likely.

art.rod.pensar.p2.text: The same analysis has to serve the board and the technical team – that is translating between levels. And the outline that organises the reasoning before the first sentence is a thinking draft.

art.rod.pensar.p3.text: They are two of the four capabilities of the Reason domain – hence the green, the same as in the domain grid. They are also the only ones that cut across all the other domains, and it is precisely because they produce no deliverable that Rodrigo had never used them.

art.rod.pensar.q.text: A thinking tool, made on purpose not to appear in the final product.

art.rod.conf.p1.text: A human expert has presumed credit. The machine does not get that benefit of the doubt when the matter is fact.

art.rod.conf.i1.text: Ground in sources – supply the documents instead of expecting the AI to invent them.

art.rod.conf.i2.text: Check separately – a second pass lists the claims and confronts them with the original.

art.rod.conf.i3.text: Know where it ends – recognise the point at which the model stops knowing and starts supposing.

art.rod.conf.q.text: Zero hallucination is not a promise of perfection. It is the refusal to accept an error without having confronted it.

art.rod.escolha.p1.text: It is not brand preference. It is what each task demands from the flow layer – and how much raw material it tolerates receiving.

art.rod.escolha.f1v2.text: A checkable source for every claim

art.rod.escolha.f1v3.text: Plenty – the raw text already serves

art.rod.escolha.f1w.text: A thesis survives a lack of formatting: what cannot be missing is a solid argument. Here it is worth trading convenience for rigour.

art.rod.escolha.f2v2.text: Access to the data where it lives

art.rod.escolha.f2v3.text: Little – the research just has to come citable

art.rod.escolha.f2w.text: The flow requirement here is about being able to check, not about appearance: research delivered, grounded and ready to cite.

art.rod.escolha.f3v3.text: None – any touch-up is a failure

art.rod.escolha.f3w.text: When only the finished result counts, the contest is too tight to declare a winner. Any revision of the scores could flip the order – and that is information, not noise.

art.rod.balanco.a1.text: One AI for everything, chosen from a list of the best

art.rod.balanco.a2.text: Asked for deliverables, never for thinking

art.rod.balanco.d1.text: Tool chosen by what the task demands

art.rod.balanco.d3.text: Grounds in sources and checks separately

art.rod.balanco.d4.text: Accepts friction where it costs nothing, refuses it where it costs

art.rod.balanco.q.text: Before, Rodrigo used AI to finish tasks. After, he started using it to begin them.

art.mar.hero.title.text: Finding is half the work: the right AI when everything needs a source.

art.mar.hero.lede.text: A narrative of applying "Quando é Melhor com IA" to a single project

art.mar.ato0.p1.text: Marina Peçanha had eleven weeks and a board of directors waiting.

art.mar.ato0.p2.text: Vitálica Saúde, a mid-sized health insurer with 380,000 members, had to decide whether to replace its claims-management core with a market platform or rebuild on the legacy system. The combined deliverable was a Decision Dossier: a grounded report, an executive deck, a navigable prototype of the claims flow and a traceability annex. Four artefacts, a single argument, a single signature at the end – hers.

art.mar.ato0.p3.text: In the first two weeks, Marina did what almost everyone does: she picked the AI with the highest score in the public comparisons and started using it for everything. The reasoning was excellent. The delivery was not. She ended her days exhausted by a kind of work she could not name.

art.mar.ato0.p4.text: The book named it. Section 5.1 (Competence and convenience as orthogonal vectors) calls it the synthetic IQ fallacy: believing that a high score in reasoning tests translates automatically into delivered productivity. The text offers the exact image of what Marina was living – the brilliant lawyer who refuses to file petitions in the format the court accepts, the engineer able to solve any algorithm but unable to read his own company's repository. The passage's conclusion is harsh, and it was what made her stop: power that does not show up in delivery is, for the corporate user, non-existent.

art.mar.ato0.p5.text: Marina realised she did not have a tool-selection problem. She had a work-architecture problem.

art.mar.ato1.h.text: Measure the friction before fighting it

art.mar.ato1.p1.text: Section 5.2 (The end of glue work) names the enemy: the "glue" work a human has to do whenever two tools do not connect natively – copying output into the editor, reformatting a table for the corporate spreadsheet, manually re-sending a file the AI should have accessed on its own.

art.mar.ato1.p2.text: Marina did something the book does not ask for explicitly, but which follows from its thesis: she timed it. For five days she logged every manual bridge. The result was 6h40 a week spent only on re-pasting, reformatting and re-sending. None of those hours had produced a single new argument.

art.mar.ato1.p3.text: Then came the diagnosis proper, with the three axes of enablement (5.3):

art.mar.ato1.li1.text: Data Gravity – does the AI operate where the corporate data lives, or does it require the user to extract it and bring it in by hand? Marina's tool required it. Every manual upload of the 340 files in the claims repository was, in the book's words, an opportunity for forgetting, staleness or the undue exclusion of relevant context.

art.mar.ato1.li2.text: Format Continuity – is the output a draft in running text to be entirely reassembled, or a final, editable artefact ready for review rather than reconstruction? The 18 slides of the deck were being rebuilt by hand from running text.

art.mar.ato1.li3.text: Trustworthiness & Verifiability – is every factual statement traceable to a verifiable source? The section makes clear that this axis is the mature, cross-cutting form of the Zero Hallucination of 6.4 and of the grounding patterns of 7.3, and it rules: a strategic synthesis without auditability is merely an opinion.

art.mar.ato1.p4.text: Marina wrote that sentence on a card and stuck it to her monitor. A dossier the board could not audit would be an expensive opinion.

art.mar.ato2.h.text: Allocate by phase, not by preference

art.mar.ato2.p1.text: The methodological turn came from the Cross-Impact Matrix (5.4), which classifies each crossing of domain and enablement axis as Critical, Supporting or Neutral. Marina read the matrix horizontally and reorganised the whole project on top of it:

art.mar.ato2.td1.text: Source survey and reading of the legacy

art.mar.ato2.td4.text: Tool connected to the internal repository, with line-by-line citation

art.mar.ato2.td8.text: Accept running text without complaint; demand the origin of every concept

art.mar.ato2.td12.text: Only a tool that returned a native, editable file

art.mar.ato2.td16.text: Tool that reads the repository and delivers as a commit

art.mar.ato2.p2.text: What sustains this reallocation is section 5.5 (Asymmetric dependence): friction does not penalise all cognitive work equally. Pure reasoning survives in raw text, because the value of an idea lies in its logical structure, not in its packaging. Execution, on the other hand, depends structurally on the delivery infrastructure – code that does not talk to the real repository is not "almost ready", it is unusable.

art.mar.ato2.p3.text: The practical gain was immediate and counter-intuitive: Marina stopped fighting the friction of the reasoning tool. In the weeks of building the thesis, she agreed to receive everything as running text, unformatted, and saved the days she would have spent migrating that work to a more "comfortable" environment. The friction she had been fighting was, in that domain, irrelevant.

art.mar.ato2.p4.text: For the operational backbone, the book supplied the skeleton of each front. Fractal symmetry (3.7) establishes that the cycle Ingestion → Transformation → Delivery repeats, identical in form, inside each domain. Marina began planning each week with three explicit blocks instead of one diffuse block called "move the project forward".

art.mar.ato3.p1.text: The legacy was 340 documents: contracts with providers, specifications of the current platform, three purchased market studies and the tender of a competitor that had made the same migration.

art.mar.ato3.p2.text: Here Marina recognised herself in the Signal Hunter (8.6) – the investigator who extracts informational truth from seas of raw data, demanding total traceability and rejecting any synthetic statement without a clear link to a real source. The book notes that this is the archetype in which Zero Hallucination shows up in its most literal and non-negotiable form.

art.mar.ato3.p3.text: The technique came from 6.5 (Detailed summaries of complex books and articles), which describes models able to ingest an entire long text and produce structured summaries, identifying key points and arguments per chapter, as well as extracting inferences that relate ideas from distant parts of the text. Marina used exactly the formulation the section suggests – questions addressed to the document, such as "what are the main points of chapter 3?" and "how does this report define metric X?" – to sweep the provider contracts for data-portability clauses.

art.mar.ato3.p4.text: She found one. Clause 14.3 of a 2019 contract, which imposed a per-record extraction cost. On its own, that clause moved the cost estimate of the "buy" option by R$ 2.1 million. No human on the team would have found it in eleven weeks.

art.mar.ato3.p5.text: The quality standard for ingestion came from 6.4 (Complete studies and reports based on reliable sources): first retrieve the relevant content, then build the synthesis on those real texts, without inventing references. And the stance came from 9.2 (Zero hallucination: the posture of proactive scepticism), with its practical rule: every factual statement by the AI is suspect until proven otherwise. A human expert enjoys presumed credibility; the AI gets no such benefit of the doubt in matters of fact. Marina applied the three practices the section prescribes – grounding, cross-checking and scope awareness –, and the second of them caught the error that would have destroyed her credibility: an industry loss ratio, quoted with absolute conviction, that existed in no primary source.

art.mar.ato3.prov.text: The two colours of this page's thread come from the AI Strategy Hub engine: in the Signal Hunter preset, Gemini leads with 4.2627 and, among the three brands the series colours, second is Claude, with 2.8991 – computed on 18·08·2026, engine v13.7, over the current evaluation matrix. What the piece argues is the separation of roles between who reads and who checks, not the choice of a product.

art.mar.ato4.p1.text: With the material grounded, Marina moved to the thesis. Here she became a Scenario Oracle (8.4) – the profile that uses AI as a high-level dialectical partner, simulating scenarios and building visions of the future grounded in rigorous deductive logic. The book places this archetype at the purest end of the Craftsman: what matters is the quality of the reasoning delivered as running text, and any demand for polished formatting is irrelevant next to the robustness of the argument.

art.mar.ato4.p2.text: Marina built the analysis prompt from the typical analytical components (7.2) – market, competitors, value chain, critical capabilities, emerging technologies and recommendations –, exactly as the section demonstrates in the residential solar energy example. The output came organised in corresponding sections, and the gain was what the book promises: completeness, the guarantee that no important angle was left out.

art.mar.ato4.p3.text: The grounding patterns (7.3) governed both halves of the work. With internal files, the focus was to maximise the use of the sources and keep them as factual ballast, with the explicit instruction the section recommends: preferably use the data provided, avoid unfounded assumptions and highlight contradictions between sources. Without files – in the market projections for 2029 –, the focus was to delimit and justify, with a closed temporal and geographical scope and with the follow-up question the book suggests: "what is the basis for this statement about market growth?". The section adds the practice that paid off most: make the AI spell out its premises and hypotheses. That is how Marina discovered that the projection most favourable to the "build" option assumed regulatory stability for five years – a premise she, aware of the ongoing coverage-list review, could knock down.

art.mar.ato4.p4.text: And here the meta-cases (Ch. 4) stopped being theory. Section 4.6 describes exactly the mental decomposition Marina began doing before each session: first ask for the integration of the sources (A – Curation, normalisation and integration), then the generation of alternatives and the critique of each (B – Logical validation and stress-test), then the translation of the best alternative into an operational plan (C – Conversion between levels of abstraction) and, finally, the checklist (D – Intermediate artefacts). Section 7.4 confirms that, in the strategic-synthesis case, all four are activated almost inevitably – the difference lies in doing it deliberately.

art.mar.ato4.p5.text: Meta-case C produced the most praised item of the dossier. The book defines it, in 3.6, as part of the cognitive substrate – not a silo of analytical reasoning, but the operating system running silently beneath every discipline. Marina used it to produce three versions of the same argument: one for the board, one for the operations directorate and one for the engineering team. Same thesis, three altitudes. None of them a summary of another.

art.mar.ato5.p1.text: The final phase demanded of Marina three identities she would not have assumed without Chapter 8.

art.mar.ato5.p2.text: For the deck, she became a Corporate Showrunner (8.3) – the orchestrator who turns abstract business visions into consumable multimodal assets, with a balanced position on the enablement spectrum, because the final delivery is itself an artefact of executive consumption. Section 6.1 (Automated generation of slide presentations) supported the flow, and the Format Continuity axis of 5.3 imposed the selection criterion: only a tool that returned a native, editable file would do.

art.mar.ato5.p3.text: For the finishing in the house template, she became an Elite Bureaucrat (8.5) – the last-mile professional for whom zero formatting errors and absolute conformity to the identity manual are not luxuries but requirements. The book describes it as the Operator in its most extreme form: for this profile, any residual copy-and-paste activity is a system failure. Marina, who prided herself on being a craftswoman, had to accept that on the Friday before the board, craftsmanship was a defect.

art.mar.ato5.p4.text: For the navigable prototype of the claims flow, she became an Agile Prototyper (8.7) – materialising abstract ideas into iterative functional prototypes to validate hypotheses at high speed. The technical basis came from 6.7 (Generation of web applications and coding automation). The prototype was what made the difference in the room: instead of describing the reduction from 9 to 4 steps in the authorisation flow, she let the board click.

art.mar.ato5.p5.text: What unifies the three identities is the synthesis of the Craftsman–Operator spectrum (5.7): maturity lies not in choosing a side once and for all, but in recognising, at each piece of work, which side it benefits from. In eleven weeks, Marina crossed the entire spectrum – three times.

art.mar.ato6.p1.text: The Decision Dossier recommended buying, with three conditions.

art.mar.ato6.p2.text: The economic defence did not come from the licence price. It came from 5.6 (The economics of friction: ROI, vendor lock-in and opacity), whose thesis Marina transposed to the platform decision: the real return should not be measured by the nominal cost of the licence, but by the opportunity cost that friction introduces – the time spent correcting poorly grounded outputs, reformatting raw deliveries, manually reconnecting systems that should talk natively. She presented that invisible tax in analyst-hours per month, with the line from the book the independent director asked her to repeat: a solution of high power and low efficiency is not an under-used innovation, it is an operational loss disguised as modernisation.

art.mar.ato6.p3.text: The first two conditions came from the same section. Vendor lock-in: the deep integration that eliminates glue work tends to lock the organisation into a single supplier, and present convenience competes with future flexibility for the same decision budget. Opacity: the more fluid and automatic the operation on files and processes, the greater the risk that changes cease to be traceable, eroding precisely the auditability the Trustworthiness & Verifiability axis demands. Marina required an exit clause with a cost ceiling and an immutable audit trail. The second was approved unanimously.

art.mar.ato6.p4.text: The third condition came from 9.4 (Privacy, security and sensitive data) and 9.5 (Intellectual property and responsible use): no identifiable member data would travel through an AI tool outside the contracted perimeter, and the claims-prioritisation model would undergo a bias review before any pilot, because applying models to decisions that affect people calls for redoubled attention so as not to reproduce discrimination.

art.mar.ato6.p5.text: On the eve, Marina ran the whole dossier through the quality checklist for deliverables (9.6), item by item, answering "OK" or "Adjustment needed": factual and source verification, integrity and completeness, logical coherence, clarity and style, spelling and formatting, privacy and sensitivity. Three items came back as "Adjustment needed". One of them was a market statistic without a checked original source – a survivor of six rounds of review.

art.mar.ato6.p6.text: The traceability annex, inspired by the logic of the matrices in Chapter 10, cross-referenced every statement in the report with its source and with the section where it was developed. The board did not open the annex. That was exactly why it approved.

art.mar.epilogo.p1.text: Marina did not get faster because she used AI. She got faster because she stopped using it in a single way.

art.mar.epilogo.p2.text: The measurable gain was the 6h40 a week of glue work she eliminated where the friction was critical – and, more importantly, the hours she stopped trying to eliminate where the friction was irrelevant. The non-measurable gain was clause 14.3, the regulatory premise knocked down, the invented loss ratio that never reached the board.

art.mar.epilogo.p3.text: What the book delivered was not a set of prompt tricks. It was a criterion: knowing, at each task, whether the problem was one of power or of efficiency – and, knowing, choosing.
